correctness.rationale: For an invariant compactly supported history measure and any \(C^1\) cylinder \(H(X_0)\), differentiating invariance gives \(\mathbb E[H'(X_0)(-\gamma X_0+\beta f(X_{-\tau}))]=0\). Since \(H'\) may be any continuous test function on the compact one-time range, this is exactly the displayed conditional regression. Time-shift invariance equates the delayed and current marginals. Writing \(V=\beta f(X_{-\tau})-\gamma X_0\), the regression gives \(\mathbb E[V\mid X_0]=0\), so the cross term vanishes and yields the variance-defect identity. If the defect is zero, invariance plus continuity forces trajectories in the support to be constant. The Lipschitz variance bound \(\operatorname{Var}(f(X))\le L^2\operatorname{Var}(X)\) then gives \(\beta L>\gamma\) for any non-equilibrium stationary state. Fresh root solving reproduces \(0.7356331448588915\), \(0.8457944676553084\), and \(1.3248837608752875\).
